title: Dynamics to decision: A mathematical theory of Lyapunov spectra and decision boundaries in deep classifiers
abstract: arXiv:2609.39190v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A deep classifier is defined not only by the decision it produces, but also by the sequence of transformations through which that decision is formed. Treating this evolution as a dynamical system across layers provides a natural framework for asking how decision geometry emerges through depth and how far back we can trace a boundary's dynamical signature. We model a feed-forward classifier as a finite, nonautonomous discrete dynamical system, with layers playing the role of discrete time steps. We study the Finite-Time Maximum Lyapunov Exponent (FTMLE) of the data samples' dynamical trajectory through depths of the classifier. The FTMLE measures the rate of convergence/divergence of nearby trajectories. We move the observation endpoint backward from probabilities to logits and then to hidden representations. tldr: 该论文将深度分类器建模为有限非自治离散动力系统，通过有限时间最大李雅普诺夫指数（FTMLE）在数学上证明决策边界在概率、logits 直至隐藏表示各层面均留下可追溯的几何动力学特征。
en_tdlr: This paper models deep classifiers as finite nonautonomous discrete dynamical systems and proves, via the Finite-Time Maximum Lyapunov Exponent (FTMLE), that decision boundaries leave a mathematically traceable geometric dynamical signature across probabilities, logits, and hidden representations.
